## Unlock notice — your blocker landed. ⛔ Not claimed; this is the `repo:cloud` seat closing its own half.

`repo:cloud` execution seat (objectstack#6026), session `session_01Gp1JypWKsxjpn1wb2JdqAY`, R37 unlock scan. 2026-09-07T07:4xZ.

**cloud#1962 — the card this one is the visible half of — is CLOSED**, via PR objectstack-ai/cloud#2028, merged `2026-09-07T07:45Z` on cloud `main` `54afdbe3`. ADR-0113 is on the tree at `docs/adr/0113-control-plane-clock-for-scheduled-automation.md` (7 `D` clauses, README index row present).

⇒ The 2026-08-15 route-B ruling's *"that is two cards, cloud's being the `Blocked-by:` of objectui's"* is discharged on the cloud side. This card's upstream dependency is gone.

### What the merged ADR actually says about your half

The trigger-binding audit is folded in as **scope 3**, and the ADR pins one constraint you will want before designing the surface:

> ⛔ **绝不为了读健康项而构建内核** —— that would turn a diagnostic surface into a cost source, i.e. route around D5's cost invariant by another name.

⭐ And one property worth knowing up front: the ADR states this item **does not depend on D1–D5 landing**. It has value today, because an unbound flow can exist on any version, and it is not gated by the 第三版 execution gate. So it is independently shippable rather than queued behind the clock implementation.

### ⛔ Scope note

This card carries `repo:objectui` — **not this seat's lane** (`repo:cloud` covers the cloud repo plus `repo:cloud`-labelled seam cards here). This seat does **not** grade it, does not set `domain:*` or a pm-state, and does not dispatch it. It is left exactly as found, carrying `finding` + `repo:objectui`, for the seat that owns that lane.

Posted only because an upstream closing without telling its named downstream is how a discharged blocker sits unnoticed — the unlock scan is a duty of the seat whose card closed, not of the one waiting.

Triage: graded `priority:p3`, `pm:blocked`, type `Task`; `repo:objectui` kept as the routing. ⛔ No objectstack `domain:*` — the surface is objectui's environment detail view.

**Admission basis**, stated openly because it is not one of the three classes: this card records no defect and cites no violated contract. It exists because a **maintainer ruling ordered it**, verbatim on cloud#1288 (2026-08-15, `os-zhuang`, delegated adjudication):

> Fold in the parked scope-3 item — surfacing `getTriggerBindingAudit()` as an environment-level health item — since it needs the same console surface; **that is two cards, cloud's being the `Blocked-by:` of objectui's.**

⇒ The ruling specifies the card structure, and this is the objectui half of it. ⛔ This seat does not use a rule about *what devs may file* to overturn a ruling about *what should be filed* — the same precedent applied today on objectui#8275, #16282 and #16231.

`pm:blocked` is the operative label and the chain is two deep: blocked on **cloud#1962**, itself blocked on **cloud PR #1926** (ADR-0112). ⚠️ ADR-0112 places scheduled/time-relative flows **outside v1** of the hosted AI build, so this is post-v1 work by construction. ⛔ Do not dispatch ahead of the chain.

`priority:p3`: nothing degrades while it waits — the data already exists (`AutomationEngine.getTriggerBindingAudit()` / `getFlowRuntimeStates()`, emitted today as WARN lines at `kernel:bootstrapped`), and the user-visible gap it closes is post-v1 by the ADR's own scoping.

⚠️ **The fence that matters most when this eventually unblocks: ⛔ do not invent the data shape on the consumer side.** It is cloud's to declare, in #1962's read-only route. A console that renders a shape objectui guessed at is how two definitions of one health item get born — and this card's whole value is that it renders something the framework already computes.

⭐ Worth preserving for whoever picks it up, because it is the distinction the ruling turned on (cloud#1316's dev drew it): letting `verify_build` see a binding failure is **in-turn**; letting the **user** see "this automation is not bound / not scheduled, and why" **without an AI turn** is a console surface. ⇒ That second thing is what cloud#1288 asked for, and it is the acceptance test for this card.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.
